title: Advanced Spectroscopy Peak Interactive Viewer with Scoring
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that implements an advanced spectroscopy peak interactive viewer with a scoring system. The scene simulates an IR/UV-Vis spectroscopy workbench where users identify, label, and score peaks on a 3D spectrum.

## Scene Setup
- Use a dark background (0x0a0a1a). Set up an OrthographicCamera looking down the Z-axis so the spectrum is rendered as a 3D ribbon in the XY plane.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light from (5,10,7) with intensity 0.8.
- The spectrum is a 3D ribbon mesh (width along X from 400nm to 4000nm mapped to world X range -12 to 12, height along Y representing absorbance 0.0-1.0 mapped to world Y range 0 to 8). Use a ShaderMaterial that colors the ribbon by wavelength (violet at 400nm through red at 700nm, then gray for IR region >700nm).
- Generate exactly 8 predefined peaks as Gaussian curves summed together. Peak centers (in nm): [520, 680, 1050, 1650, 2100, 2850, 3200, 3650]. Peak heights (absorbance): [0.85, 0.62, 0.45, 0.78, 0.33, 0.91, 0.55, 0.70]. Peak widths (sigma in nm): [30, 25, 60, 40, 80, 35, 50, 45]. The total spectrum curve is the sum of all 8 Gaussians.
- Render the spectrum curve as a thick Line2 or TubeGeometry on top of the ribbon.
- Draw grid lines on the background: vertical lines every 500nm, horizontal lines every 0.2 absorbance units. Label axes: X-axis 'Wavelength (nm)', Y-axis 'Absorbance'.

## Peak Markers & Interaction
- When the user clicks on the spectrum curve (raycasting against the ribbon mesh), place a vertical marker (a thin cylinder or line, colored yellow, height=full Y range) at the clicked X position. Convert the click X back to wavelength.
- If the clicked wavelength is within ±1.5*sigma of any peak center, it counts as a HIT. The marker turns green. If outside all peak tolerances, it is a MISS and the marker turns red.
- Each peak can only be identified once. Clicking near an already-identified peak does nothing (marker not placed).
- On a HIT, calculate accuracy as: accuracy = 1.0 - (|clickedWavelength - peakCenter| / (1.5 * sigma)). Score for that peak = Math.round(accuracy * 100). Add to total score.

## Keyboard Controls
- 'Z' key: Undo the last placed marker (remove it, restore peak to unidentified if it was a HIT, subtract its score). Support up to 8 levels of undo.
- 'Y' key: Redo the last undone action (re-place marker, re-identify peak, re-add score).
- 'R' key: Reset all markers, scores, and identified peaks to initial state.
- Arrow Left/Right: Pan the camera along X by 1 unit per press.
- Arrow Up/Down: Zoom in/out by adjusting the orthographic camera bounds by ±0.5 per press. Clamp zoom so frustum half-height stays between 2 and 12.
- 'H' key: Toggle a hint overlay that shows faint dashed vertical lines at all unidentified peak centers (toggling hints costs 50 points deducted from total score, only deducted on first toggle-on, not on toggle-off or subsequent toggles).

## DOM HUD Elements
- A top-left panel (id='hud-panel') showing: Score (id='score-display'), Peaks Found (id='peaks-found', format 'X/8'), Accuracy of last hit (id='last-accuracy').
- A bottom bar (id='wavelength-bar') showing the current mouse hover wavelength (id='hover-wavelength') updated on mousemove.
- A button (id='btn-reset') that triggers the same reset as 'R' key.
- A button (id='btn-hint') that triggers the same hint toggle as 'H' key.
- A completion banner (id='completion-banner', initially hidden with display:none) that appears when all 8 peaks are found, showing final score.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame or on event:
- peakCenters: [520, 680, 1050, 1650, 2100, 2850, 3200, 3650] (constant array)
- peakHeights: [0.85, 0.62, 0.45, 0.78, 0.33, 0.91, 0.55, 0.70] (constant array)
- peakSigmas: [30, 25, 60, 40, 80, 35, 50, 45] (constant array)
- identifiedPeaks: array of booleans length 8, true if that peak has been identified
- peaksFoundCount: integer 0-8
- totalScore: integer
- lastAccuracy: number 0.0-1.0 or null if no hit yet
- markers: array of objects {wavelength: number, isHit: boolean, peakIndex: number|null, score: number}
- markerCount: integer
- undoStack: array (the undo history)
- redoStack: array (the redo history)
- undoStackSize: integer
- redoStackSize: integer
- hintsActive: boolean
- hintPenaltyApplied: boolean
- cameraX: number (camera center X position)
- zoomLevel: number (orthographic frustum half-height)
- hoverWavelength: number|null
- allPeaksFound: boolean
- completionBannerVisible: boolean

Ensure all numerical values are NaN-free. Clamp all scores to non-negative. The scoring system must be deterministic given the same click positions.
physics_constraints: Gaussian peak model: absorbance(λ) = Σ height_i * exp(-0.5*((λ - center_i)/sigma_i)^2). Hit detection tolerance: |clickedλ - center_i| <= 1.5 * sigma_i. Accuracy = 1.0 - (|clickedλ - center_i| / (1.5 * sigma_i)). Score per peak = round(accuracy * 100). Total score is sum of all peak scores minus any hint penalty (50 points, applied once). All scores clamped >= 0. Maximum possible score without hints = 800. Undo/redo must perfectly restore all state.
